summary.name: Grux
summary.one_liner: Grux is a free, open source macOS menu bar AI agent that reads your active window and works with your mail, calendar, contacts and files, using either your own Anthropic API key or a local Ollama model.
use_cases: Ask questions about the window you are currently working in
Take local meeting notes with speaker attribution
Draft mail replies using your mail, calendar and contacts
Check which local Ollama models fit your Mac's memory
Run shell commands with approval before anything risky executes
Review a log of what you worked on during the day
summary.what_it_does: Grux is a macOS menu bar assistant with a single Command Panel for chat, mail, calendar, contacts and files. It can read the active window for context, so you do not need to paste screenshots. Meetings can be recorded from the microphone and system audio, with the transcript built on the Mac. A Local Models feature reads your hardware and rates which Ollama models will run well. Shell commands run against a denylist inside folders you choose, and sensitive actions wait in an Approvals queue. Every tool attempt, including refusals, is written to a plain text log on your disk.
notable: Runs fully local with Ollama, with no data leaving the machine
Approvals queue stops sensitive shell, network, delete or spend actions until you confirm
Security guardrail package is separate, MIT licensed, with 125 tests and published advisories disclosed
Meeting transcription done on-device with speaker attribution
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon
Needs your own Anthropic API key or a local Ollama install; model costs are paid directly to the provider
Not sandboxed, and the security boundary is a Swift file rather than the operating system; the page notes some permissions are not checked before use
Six published GitHub advisories against earlier releases of the guardrail package, two critical
